messages:
maya: throwing up a rough design for adaptive checkpoints for a unified paginate/stream primitive. Aim: let apps choose low-latency streaming but still optionally recover from failures with bounded rework. want feedback on semantics + transport-level details.
sam: tl;dr: good idea. question: how do we avoid replaying expensive server-side work on resume? need server-provided processed-offset + client work-id so server can no-op duplicates.
ben: ergonomics: keep client APIs tiny and consistent across languages. my thought: a single `client.iter()` that yields {value, meta}. meta can contain checkpoint info occasionally. languages map: TS -> AsyncIterable<{value,meta}>, Py -> async generator, Go -> receive-only chan Item.
lia: also consider adaptive checkpoint frequency based on observed failure rate and latency. e.g., checkpoint_every defaults to 32 but client can pass adaptive: true and server will make it more frequent under load. that reduces wasted work.
maya: concrete sketch:
- API: client.iter(req, {mode: "paged" | "stream" | "adaptive", resume: "opt-in" | "never", desired_checkpoint_size: int, retry: RetryCfg})
- Behavior: stream: no checkpoints, lowest latency; paged: existing opaque pages; adaptive: items emitted as stream but server issues checkpoint tokens periodically and the SDK surfaces them in meta.resume_cursor when available.
- Resume semantics: resume allowed only when resume=opt-in, and only from the last observed resume_cursor. resume requests include header `X-RW-Cursor` and `X-RW-Job` (job is server work identifier). server responds with `processed_offset` and may dedup.

TS example:
```ts
for await (const {value, meta} of client.iter({q: '...'}, {mode: 'adaptive', resume: 'opt-in', desired_checkpoint_size: 16})) {
  if (meta?.resume_cursor) {
    // apps can persist meta.resume_cursor
  }
}
```
Go example:
```go
ch := client.Iter(ctx, req, Opts{Mode: Adaptive, Resume: OptIn, CheckpointSize:16})
for item := range ch {
  // item.Meta.ResumeCursor maybe set occasionally
}
```
Python:
```py
async for rec in client.iter(req, mode='adaptive', resume='opt-in', desired_checkpoint_size=16):
    # rec['meta'].get('resume_cursor')
```

ben: transport note: runtime should hide HTTP/2 vs grpc. but the cursor and job headers must be normalized. suggest header names above and also include them in the JSON body for transports that can't set headers reliably (e.g., websockets/proxied envs). so resume token appears both in header `X-RW-Cursor` and in response envelope `resume_cursor` for portability.
sam: retries: policy semantics need to be explicit in docs. my proposal:
- If no checkpoint observed: SDK will perform immediate retries per RetryCfg (idempotency required), but will not attempt resume (because no safe checkpoint).
- If checkpoint observed: on fatal transport error, SDK will surface an error to app with the last_checkpoint included and also attempt an automatic resume up to resume_retries attempts using the cursor. Automatic resume uses idempotency key header `X-RW-Idempotency` + `X-RW-Job` to help server dedup.
lia: server-side: implement best-effort dedup by (job, offset) and an LRU cache of recent idempotency keys. docs must state duplicates are still possible for non-idempotent side effects. also consider server returning `replayed: true` in resumed response for telemetry.
olga: compatibility: old `paginate()` callers should keep behavior unchanged. propose adding `client.iter().stream()` and `client.iter().page()` helpers for migration; default remains paged to avoid surprising users.
ci-bot: ci: integration-tests/hybrid-checkpoint passed on hybrid-checkpoint branch (build 4982) :white_check_mark:
maya: next actions: I'll draft RFC with: exact header names (X-RW-Cursor, X-RW-Job, X-RW-Idempotency), JSON envelope fields (resume_cursor, processed_offset, replayed), error codes for resumeable vs non-resumeable failures, and SDK snippets per language. owners: maya (lead), ben (sdk), lia (server), sam (perf probes). @olga please add UX notes about persisting cursors in localStorage vs server side?
olga: will do a short UX blurb. also will add example migration guide.
maya: ok thanks all. I'll link the RFC here once created. if anyone has objections to header names or the opt-in resume semantics, flag before EOD.
